newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean soldiers beat, threaten foreign reporters.
newsitem.headline: Zairean soldiers beat, threaten foreign reporters.

text.p: Zairean troops beat and threatened to kill four foreign reporters in the second city Lubumbashi before it fell this week, the journalists said on Friday.

Around 10 soldiers from the special presidential division DSP detained correspondents from Reuters news agency, the British Broadcasting Corporation and London's Guardian newspaper agency and a freelance Belgian journalist on Tuesday.
The journalists -- three men and a woman -- said they were hit about the face and head. The soldiers then loaded a rifle and told them to say their last prayers because they were about to die.
The soldiers also stripped, beat and kicked a local translator with the journalists, accusing him of selling his country.
Intervention from the SNIP security police calmed the situation, and after several hours the journalists and translator were allowed to go, minus car and cameras.
Rebels took the city on Wednesday. Some of the DSP soldiers flew to Kinshasa but most fled into the nearby bush. REUTER
